close_reason: IdentityProvider trait extracted as supertrait of FederationTransport. ConnectionContext replaces bare SocketAddr. TailscaleIdentityProvider implemented as standalone + composed in TailscaleTransport. All 1,197 tests pass.
description: kith hardcodes Tailscale WhoIs as the sole identity source. The transport trait (KITH-lhaj) abstracts the network layer but identity verification is a separate concern — 'how did this connection get here' vs 'who is the person on the other end'. Extract an identity provider trait: trait IdentityProvider { fn verify(conn) -> Identity }. Implementations: (1) Tailscale WhoIs (current), (2) X.509 client certificate (mTLS — extract CN/SAN, validate against CA), (3) OIDC/SAML bearer token (for eduroam/InCommon/Keycloak deployments), (4) DID resolution (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-did-00), (5) PIV/CAC smart card certificate (DoD PKI — same as X.509 but with specific CA roots and OID validation). The identity provider is orthogonal to transport: you can run X.509 identity over Tailscale transport, or OIDC identity over DNS+mTLS transport. The trait should return the same Identity struct that kith already uses (user_id, login_name, display_name, node_name) regardless of provider.
title: Pluggable identity provider abstraction
